releases.body:
### Added
- GPT-6.1 Terra (`gpt-6.1-terra`) with `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, and `ultra` efforts. It has its own model family and prompt cache (and no auto-fallback chain), uses responses-lite, and ships in both config templates with a `low` default. The catalog now covers 12 bases and 65 variants. ([#299](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/299), thanks @WarGloom)
- Codex Fast tier. A host `serviceTier`, the new per-model or global `serviceTier` option (`fast`/`priority`, `flex`, `default`), or a `-fast` model id now sends `service_tier: "priority"` to models whose Codex catalog entry offers it. Before this, `gpt-5.5-fast` was only an alias. `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` default to Fast as in stock Codex, and `serviceTier: "default"` opts out. The tier is re-resolved on model fallback. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))
- Codex 0.166 request headers: `x-codex-routing-hint`, `session-id`/`thread-id` (sent alongside the legacy `session_id`/`conversation_id`), `version` under the Codex CLI identity, and `x-codex-turn-state` sticky routing. The turn-state token is replayed within a turn and on same-account retries. It is tracked per session and account, and dropped at the next user message. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))

### Changed
- `ultra` now resolves the way Codex does: to the catalog's multi-agent effort, which is `xhigh` on `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, and `gpt-6.1-terra`, and to `max` elsewhere. Native mode now applies the same effort clamps as legacy mode, so `ultra` never reaches the wire. ([#299](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/299), [#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))
- Request shape follows Codex 0.166. No request carries a top-level `instructions` field; base instructions are the first developer message in `input`. Responses-lite groups function and custom tools into the `functions` namespace and skips `additional_tools` when a turn has no tools. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))
- `text.verbosity` falls back to the Codex catalog default (`low`; `high` on Daybreak Red) in both modes. An explicit `reasoningSummary: "none"`/`"off"` now omits the field instead of becoming `auto`. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))
- Shipped templates advertise the Codex working context window: 272000, or 500000 for `gpt-6.1-terra`, instead of 1050000/872000. OpenCode now compacts when Codex would. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))

### Fixed
- OpenCode V2 requests now carry `prompt_cache_key`, plus the matching `session_id`/`conversation_id`, derived from the session-affinity headers. The host's AI SDK bridge drops `promptCacheKey`, so tool-result continuations used to miss the prompt cache. Provider-configured affinity headers are honored too. ([#296](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/issues/296), [#297](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/297))
- A plain-string `input` is no longer dropped when instructions or `additional_tools` are prepended. ([#300](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/300))


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/compare/v6.29.0...v6.30.0

### Added
- Custom rotation policies: `rotationStrategy: "custom"` runs a user-supplied `.mjs` `select` module in a bounded child process (four-way concurrency cap, 1 MiB input, 64 KiB output, one-second selection deadline) with environment and preload stripped. Policies validate offline through `scripts/rotation-validate.js` against scenario fixtures, feed account-scoped quota observations into host eligibility, and ship a `/rotation` package export for the policy contract. ([#292](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/292), thanks @PENEKhun)

### Fixed
- `codex-limits` text reports now preserve every emitted field: banked reset credits render whenever the server reports them — including `0 banked`, previously dropped — and the tool description pins complete-report semantics so agent summaries can no longer drop the 5-hour or resets columns the user asked for. ([#291](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/291), thanks @lubshad)
- Function tools sent to the Codex Responses backend now carry `strict: false` when the host left strictness unset — pinned in the shared `transformRequestForCodex` path ([#294](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/294), thanks @SteveLTN) and in the OpenCode V2 adapter's language-model hook ([#295](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/295)). An omitted flag was treated as strict mode, making optional parameters effectively required so models fabricated values like the subagent `sessionID` and fresh subagent creation failed with `Subagent session not found`. ([#293](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/issues/293))
- `runRotationPolicy` disarms the selection deadline the moment a complete result arrives, so the deadline can no longer fire inside the Windows `taskkill` teardown window and report `timeout` over a finished policy. ([#292](https://github.com/ndycode/oc-codex-multi-auth/pull/292))

https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-codex-multi-auth/v/6.28.0

```bash
npx oc-codex-multi-auth@6.28.0 install
```

## Added
- `codex-enable` (25th registered tool) re-enables a disabled account by index or picker, strips the auto-disable marker, clears its auth-failure cooldown, and reloads the cached manager — concurrent enables serialize through the shared load slot so installs land in commit order, and a rejected in-flight load no longer blocks the reload. `codex-health` and `codex-refresh` accept `includeDisabled` to validate credentials without re-enabling. (#288, #290)

## Fixed
- The OAuth `/connect` method now declares its `prompts`, so the host form collects login mode and account count instead of the plugin grabbing stdin under the host TUI (`EALREADY`). A form-driven "start fresh" also clears the flagged store with a cutoff that preserves records another runtime flags mid-login, verifies the keychain entry matches the survivors, and retires only proven-stale migration markers. (#287, #289)
- Accounts the plugin disables itself — repeated auth failures or workspace deactivation — now carry an `accountNote` marker that survives persistence and disk merges, so `codex-doctor`, `codex-status`, explainability reasons, and beginner guidance can tell auto-disabled from operator-disabled. A pool where every account is auto-disabled reports `all_accounts_disabled` instead of masquerading as a rate limit, V2 `resolveAuth` no longer selects disabled accounts, and `codex-doctor` notes when the host's own `openai` credential can still serve requests while the whole pool is disabled. (#288, #290)
- Cache invalidation now runs before flagged-store cleanup on both fresh paths, so a cleanup failure can no longer leave a stale manager able to debounced-save wiped or pre-fresh members back. (#289)

https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-codex-multi-auth/v/6.27.0

```bash
npx oc-codex-multi-auth@6.27.0 install
```

## Added
- `spendCredits` (or `CODEX_AUTH_SPEND_CREDITS=1`, default off) opts the rotation in to spending Codex credit balances once every account entitled to the model is out of plan quota. Credit candidates respect `modelAccountPools` strict/preferred pools and are ordered by largest balance; balances come from `/wham/usage` and are refreshed by `x-codex-credits-*` response headers. A refused credits turn is parked until the quota reset (default 10 minutes), a toast announces when a request is running on paid credits, and the TUI status rotation gains a `credits` screen listing funded accounts. (#286, thanks @Nowaker)

## Fixed
- `limits` — CLI, `codex-limits`, and the TUI quota view — now names the cached accounts it can no longer read: a dead refresh token or an auth-failure cooldown keeps the last known figures under a clear error line, drops the account out of pool totals, and exits nonzero, while timeouts, 429s, and 5xx responses no longer mark credentials dead and a stale reading can't erase a newer failure. (#285, thanks @Nowaker)
- A credits refusal is remembered only on an authoritative usage-limit signal — a transient 429, overload, or concurrency throttle no longer parks a funded account, and a refused turn can no longer be billed a second time by the same request's short retry. `limits --json` keeps `credits` in the raw `codex-limits` form (`"62500"`, `unlimited`, `available`) instead of the grouped display string. (#286)
- Decoded usage-error messages drop terminal control characters, so a hostile or corrupted error body can no longer inject escape sequences into `limits` output. (#285)

https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-codex-multi-auth/v/6.26.0

```bash
npx oc-codex-multi-auth@6.26.0 install
```

## Added
- Support for `gpt-6.1-sol`, the new default model in the OpenAI Codex catalog (openai/codex PR #49318, 2026-09-29): normalization with a bare `gpt-6.1` alias, its own model family and instruction slug, responses-lite request shaping, low–ultra reasoning variants in the shipped `modern`/`legacy` catalogs (now 11 bases / 59 selectors), and default fallback-chain coverage between `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6-sol`. (#284)
- `quotaNotifications.autoRedeemResets` (with `autoRedeemResetsBelowPercent`, default 10) lets the quota poll spend one banked rate-limit reset credit on an account whose weekly quota is nearly gone and the server reports the credit applicable now. (#283, thanks @yuefdev)

## Changed
- Plan labels follow the upstream Codex Pro ladder (openai/codex #47971): `prolite` → "Pro", `pro` → "Pro (More)", `promax` → "Pro (Max)"; `promax` seats report ~$500/mo with no published allotment ratio. The default Codex client version now tracks the highest catalog `minimal_client_version` (0.155.0). (#284)

## Fixed
- The quota monitor keeps polling when `autoRedeemResets` is the only enabled feature; a usage re-read failure after a successful redeem no longer leaves the account blocked, and the stale snapshot can't re-stamp the cleared block. A cross-process claim under the account-storage lock bounds auto-redeem to one spend attempt per account per week, so two hosts holding the same low-quota reading cannot each burn a credit. (#283)
- A custom fallback chain keyed `gpt-6.1` now resolves to the same `gpt-6.1-sol` node the request path normalizes to. (#284)
